papers.title: General-purpose foundation models surpass specialized ones on chemical property prediction tasks
papers.abstract: Foundation models (FMs) learn reusable representations from large collections of unlabeled data. In chemistry the corresponding data mainly consists of molecular structures, which are abundant, whereas experimental measurements are scarce. Chemical FMs such as ChemBERTa and MoLFormer were therefore trained on diverse molecular structures to enable fine-tuning on small experimental datasets (less than 100 datapoints in most realistic scenarios) and subsequent property prediction. At the same time, general-purpose FMs such as GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5 were trained on virtually all publicly available data, including knowledge of the humankind on molecular properties and laws governing them. Here we compare accuracies of chemical and general-purpose FMs on tasks from various areas of chemistry. Strikingly, general-purpose GPT-6 Astra outperforms the currently eligible chemical FMs on five physicochemical and quantum-chemical regression tasks when only 60 experimental datapoints are available. Only when provided 10x datapoints do the best chemical FMs reach performance of GPT-6 Astra: on 1,000 and 10,000 points they show performance on par with Astra on 60 and 1,000 points, respectively. Thus, counterintuitively, frontier general-purpose FMs are better suited for guiding chemical research in data-scarce areas than specialized chemical FMs, suggesting that learning relevant primitives (e.g. chemical structures) does not substitute training on relevant humankind knowledge.

papers.title: Towards Out-of-Distribution Uncertainty Quantification for Machine-Learned Interatomic Potentials via Pre-Training
papers.abstract: Informative uncertainty quantification (UQ) is essential for the practical deployment of machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs), as it provides insight into their reliability across chemical space. Although numerous post-hoc uncertainty estimation methods for MLIPs have recently been proposed, most have been trained in low-data regimes, restricting their applicability to narrow domains of interest. Inspired by the emergence of foundational MLIPs, we propose pre-training uncertainty estimators on large, diverse datasets to enable broader applicability. We pre-train several UQ models on large materials science datasets to quantify the uncertainty of different MLIPs, and evaluate their performance on both in-distribution and out-of-domain (OOD) adsorption-energy predictions. We find that pre-trained uncertainty estimators provide viable zero-shot uncertainty estimates across multiple datasets, while fine-tuning consistently yields positive correlations between predicted uncertainty and prediction error, even on the most challenging datasets. These results lay the groundwork for foundational UQ models for MLIPs, ultimately facilitating their deployment in practical settings by providing users with a priori information about model reliability and applicability.

papers.title: El Agente Quntur: Agentic Active-Space Selection for CASSCF
papers.abstract: Multireference calculations require time-consuming expert decisions about active spaces, state identity, and convergence. This study asks whether agents can make these decisions reliably. Using the El Agente Quntur multi-agent harness with GPT-5.6 Sol and GPT-5.6 Terra as its language models, agents study 32 fixed-geometry singlet excitations, detect missing active orbitals, compare excited states, and revise state assignments as calculations progress. Prompts specify equal-weight two-singlet state-averaged complete active space self-consistent field (CASSCF) calculations followed by strongly contracted second-order N-electron valence state perturbation theory (NEVPT2) with def2-TZVPD; agents choose and refine the active spaces. Excitation energies are evaluated against published complete active space second-order perturbation theory (CASPT2) reference values at matching geometries. Agentic execution reduces mean absolute error by 48\% relative to six deterministic Active Space Finder protocols. Computational traces vary substantially across runs in selection strategies and cost, even for the same molecule. These results underscore the advantage of agentic active space selection over fixed workflows, yet leave room to improve efficiency through runtime-aware decision-making, reduced inter-agent communication overhead and redundancy, more systematic checks of state identity, and clearer stopping criteria.

papers.title: Tunable Three-Body Interactions in Microwave-Shielded Polar Molecules
papers.abstract: We show that microwave shielding, which enables collisionally stable ultracold polar molecules, also leads to genuine nonadditive three-body interactions comparable to the shielding interaction itself. Their magnitude, sign, and geometrical dependence can be flexibly controlled through microwave parameters and orientation. Interaction strengths can reach the ten kilohertz-scale for ultrapolar molecules in typical optical lattices. The nonadditive three-body interactions can stabilize novel many-body phases, and should be accounted for in quantum simulation with microwave shielded molecules.

papers.title: Exact Electron Dynamics in Linear and Chiral Cavities: Complete Field versus Single-Helicity Reduction
papers.abstract: Can a chiral cavity turn a free electron into a Landau-like orbiting particle? We answer with exact solutions of three quadratic electron--cavity models in the dipole limit, valid at arbitrary coupling. A single linearly polarized mode dresses the electron mass, which delays its flight, slows the spreading of a wavepacket and entangles the packet with the cavity. The complete transverse field, with both circular helicities, keeps two commuting, gapless translations at any coupling, mode number and helicity splitting, so the electron stays ballistic and no synthetic magnetic field appears. Keeping a single helicity gives two inequivalent models that are not related by a gauge transformation: reducing before the Power--Zienau--Woolley transformation gives ballistic motion, whereas reducing after it gives a Landau-like crossed-quadrature Hamiltonian. They differ by a real uniform field $B=s\lambda^2/(2\omega_c)$ ($\omega_c$ the mode frequency, $\lambda$ the coupling, $s=\pm1$ the helicity). In the complete theory the frequency $\omega_{-s}$ of the partner helicity, measured against $g^2=\lambda^2/(2\omega_c)$, decides between them: the electron is ballistic for a stiff partner, and Landau-like only at the soft-partner point, through an exact canonical reorganization that holds for the active sector but not for observables such as the electron--photon entanglement. Projecting onto one helicity after the PZW transformation is therefore not by itself a mechanism for synthetic magnetism; the mode content of the cavity is.

papers.title: eCAS: An Orbital Embedding Method for Quantum Computing
papers.abstract: Future fault-tolerant quantum computers will allow us to calculate electronic structures of atomistic systems. However, these systems will be intrinsically limited in size, requiring embedding theories for many systems because of the unfavorable scaling of the number of terms describing the electron-electron interaction in the second-quantized electronic Hamiltonian. Quantum embedding theories address this challenge by partitioning a quantum system into a region of interest, the impurity, and its (larger) complement, the environment. However, currently available quantum embedding methods place restrictive demands on near-future quantum computers, such as the need to measure reduced density matrices or the need for repeated evaluations. Here, we introduce the new orbital embedding method eCAS that steers clear of these pitfalls by constructing a multi-CAS problem, the active spaces of which are localized and can be solved independently of each other with any quantum algorithm. This also allows for the development of comparatively simple gradient expressions. eCAS leverages the Schmidt decomposition to construct initial impurity and bath orbitals and augments them with localized environment orbitals, based on a mutual correlation criterion. The mutual correlation criterion makes eCAS systematically improvable without the need for any iteratively determined quantities.

papers.title: Electron Scattering with ASTRA: Helium and Molecular Hydrogen
papers.abstract: We present an implementation of electron-impact scattering in ASTRA, a close-coupling method based on transition density matrices previously applied to molecular photoionization. The scattering states are obtained with a pole-free Galerkin method with variational surface matching, which yields the scattering matrix and the channel-resolved amplitudes for elastic and electronically inelastic integral cross sections and molecular-frame differential cross sections. For helium, ASTRA reproduces elastic and inelastic cross sections over a broad energy range, resolves the He$^-$(1s2s$^2$ $^2$S$^e$) Feshbach resonance in both energy and angle, and captures the principal interference structures in the n=2 excitation angular distributions, in selected channels matching measured differential-cross-section ratios more closely than available benchmark calculations. For molecular hydrogen, target polarization and interchannel coupling are represented through additional close-coupling channels, without a fitted polarization potential or a separately constructed (N+1)-electron correlation space. Compared with the restricted-channel description, the expanded calculations substantially improve agreement with UKRmol+ for elastic and inelastic cross sections. We further report fully orientation-resolved three-dimensional molecular-frame angular distributions for state-resolved electron-impact excitation. These reveal pronounced stereodynamic effects that vanish upon orientational averaging: at 15 eV, excitation of the b$^3\Sigma_u^+$ state is more than eight times stronger for incident momentum parallel rather than perpendicular to the molecular axis. These results connect conventional scattering benchmarks with orientation-resolved collision dynamics and open the way to larger molecular targets.

papers.title: Physical Mechanisms of Light-Induced Molecular Fragmentation in the Long-Wavelength Regime
papers.abstract: Strong near-infrared (NIR) laser fields ionize polyatomic molecules through tunneling and multiphoton processes, while subsequent molecular fragmentation can be driven by electron rescattering and field-induced nonadiabatic excitation of the molecular ion. How these competing mechanisms deposit energy into molecular ions and determine fragmentation branching remains unresolved. By combining wavelength- and ellipticity-dependent intensity-difference mass spectrometry of methanol with time-dependent Schr\"odinger equation (TDSE) and semiclassical Monte Carlo simulations, we demonstrate that, in the tunneling-to-intermediate regime ($\gamma \lesssim 1$), molecular fragmentation is governed by the interplay of electron recollision and field-driven nonadiabatic excitation, revealing competing physical mechanisms relevant to polyatomic molecules more broadly. Ellipticity-dependent measurements demonstrate that these mechanisms can be experimentally distinguished for individual cationic fragments. Channels requiring high internal energies exhibit the strong ellipticity-dependent suppression characteristic of rescattering-driven processes, while lower-energy channels are comparatively less sensitive. Although small-fragment yields decrease substantially with increasing wavelength, their relative distributions remain largely unchanged, indicating that the underlying fragmentation pathways are preserved and that the suppression primarily reflects reduced probabilities of electron recollision and nonadiabatic excitations at longer wavelengths.

papers.title: Atomistic Emergence of Vibrational Polariton Condensation
papers.abstract: Nonequilibrium polariton condensation is a macroscopic quantum phenomenon in which overwhelming population accumulation is observed at the band edge of the lower polariton (LP) dispersion curve under incoherent material pumping. As a promising route toward nonequilibrium Bose--Einstein condensates, its description, however, remains predominantly limited to models with phenomenological material parameters. Herein, a fully atomistic description of vibrational polariton condensation is developed by employing mesoscale cavity molecular dynamics simulations, a method which self-consistently propagates classical electromagnetic dynamics coupled to realistic molecules in a multimode Fabry--P\'erot cavity. Under continuous-wave pumping, a lower polariton condensate forms when the infrared cavity is coupled to harmonic, homogeneously broadened molecular vibrations, such as the bending modes of liquid CO2 and CS2, whereas anharmonic stretching modes and liquids with fast intramolecular relaxation hardly condense. The role of libration-bending coupling for facilitating the LP condensation is further discussed. GPU-accelerated mesoscale simulations involving approximately 50 million atoms additionally provide direct two-dimensional real-space imaging of fluid-like polariton patterns during the condensation formation. Overall, this study provides key design insights into vibrational polariton condensation as a novel approach for controlling liquid-phase chemistry.

papers.title: Streptavidin-Biotin Binding is Intrinsically Non-Cooperative, but Experimental Artefacts Can Induce Apparent Positive Cooperativity
papers.abstract: The biotin-streptavidin interaction is a key component of nanobiotechnology, yet the nature of its cooperativity remains a debated question. Here, we introduce a label-free spectroscopy approach based on confocal UV autofluorescence microscopy to probe the binding cooperativity of this high-affinity system. By leveraging the intrinsic autofluorescence of tryptophan residues, we avoid artefacts associated with extrinsic fluorescent labels, enabling precise measurements of fully biotin-saturated streptavidin across a wide range of molar ratios. Our experimental results, supported by Monte Carlo simulations, provide conclusive evidence for the absence of cooperativity. However, we show that false signs of apparent positive cooperativity can emerge from local concentration inhomogeneities occurring when rapid reaction kinetics outpace mixing. By establishing the non-cooperative nature of biotin-streptavidin binding and identifying the key conditions to avoid cooperativity artefacts, these insights resolve a longstanding debate and offer critical implications for streptavidin-based biotechnological applications.

papers.title: A Hybrid Message-Passing and Electric-Field Representation for Electrostatic QM/MM Embedding with Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials
papers.abstract: Within a hybrid quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics approach a small region of a large atomistic system is described quantum mechanically, while the rest of the system is represented by a classical force field. Despite this, the computational cost of the quantum calculation severely limits the accessible simulation and sampling time. Replacing the quantum calculation with a machine learning interatomic potential (MLIP) trained on quantum reference data can greatly increase the accessible simulation time. However, the accuracy and efficiency strongly depend on the specific way in which the MLIP incorporates information about the classical (electrostatic) environment. Here, we demonstrate that existing strategies based purely on features derived from an external electric field fail to distinguish certain environments, ultimately limiting their accuracy. As a solution, we propose an extension to the equivariant TensorNet architecture that mitigates this shortcoming by incorporating classical atoms close to the quantum region into the message-passing scheme, combined with features derived from the electric field for describing the environment farther away. We show that this combination achieves higher accuracy than either approach alone.

papers.title: Surface Hopping Dynamics on Adiabatic States Propagated with Real-Time TDDFT
papers.abstract: Real-time time-dependent density functional theory (RT-TDDFT) is widely used to simulate ultrafast electron dynamics, but it is usually coupled to the nuclei through the mean-field Ehrenfest approximation, which cannot describe wavepacket branching and violates detailed balance. Surface hopping avoids these problems, but has not previously been combined with RT-TDDFT because real-time propagation does not directly provide the necessary adiabatic states. In this work we introduce an energy-scaled time-dependent Kohn--Sham (TDKS) propagation scheme, motivated by the quantum adiabatic theorem. Scaling widens the separation between electronic and nuclear timescales, so that each propagated state follows the adiabatic surface selected by its initial condition: either the ground state or a non-Aufbau self-consistent-field ($\Delta$SCF) solution. The propagation thereby avoids the convergence failures of static SCF solvers in regions of strong nonadiabatic coupling. Because the independently propagated states are complex-valued and not mutually orthogonal, we reformulate the mapping approach to surface hopping (MASH) in a complex adiabatic basis and introduce a dynamical transition orbital (DTO) gauge that restores a well-defined particle--hole representation for evaluating time-derivative couplings and nonadiabatic coupling vectors. Applied to the photoisomerization of \textit{trans}-diimide, the scheme converges systematically as the scaling factor is increased and yields an excited-state lifetime in good agreement with previous nonadiabatic simulations based on static SCF.\@ These results establish real-time propagation as an efficient and numerically stable route to the adiabatic states and couplings required for first-principles surface hopping.

papers.title: The Role of Electron-Nuclear Coupling on Chemical and Physical Processes
papers.abstract: Over the last few decades, Born-Oppenheimer (BO) and Born-Oppenheimer-Huang (BOH) treatments for electron-nuclear equation of motion have been considered as the cornerstone for qualitative as well as quantitative exploration and understanding of chemical and physical processes. The BO approximation due to the large mass difference between electrons and nuclei as well as the energy separation among the electronic states could able to predict some of the processes (chemical and physical) satisfactorily at lower energy regime. Such approximation (BO) quite often fails for those cases with the involvement of excited electronic states, in particular, due to the coupling among the states. On the other hand, the BO treatment provides two important quantities, namely, the adiabatic potential energy surfaces (PESs) and the nonadiabatic coupling terms (NACTs) determining the forces, which control the motion of the nuclei in a molecule. The NACTs play a major role in photoexcitation spectra, charge transfer chemical reactions, ferroelectric property and other processes, where significant anomalies are observed between single and multiple PES(s) results. Since the NACTs often exhibit singularity at the close vicinity of degenerate states forming conical intersections (CIs), such coupling terms could break the symmetry of the molecular processes changing the observables qualitatively.

papers.title: Estimating Irving-Kirkwood pressure profiles from per-atom virial and density profiles: a closure for the contour-dependent term in planar liquid films
papers.abstract: The local pressure tensor of an inhomogeneous fluid is not unique. Two tangential profiles are in common use in planar simulations: the Irving-Kirkwood (IK) profile, which requires a dedicated pass over every pair of atoms for every slab, and the per-atom virial (PAV) profile, which molecular-dynamics codes produce at negligible cost and coincides with the Harasima contour. The two differ by the derivative of a pair quantity, P_T^IK - P_T^PAV = dQ/dz. We show that, for Lennard-Jones free-standing films, Q(z) can be predicted from the density profile and the bulk radial distribution function of the coexisting liquid: under the closure rho2(r1,r2) ~ rho(z1) rho(z2) g(r12), with a pair-local interpolation of g between its liquid and dilute limits, Q is a double integral of rho(z) against a kernel built from u'(r) g(r). The estimator P_T^IK,est = P_T^PAV + dQ/dz is tested against IK profiles measured on the same trajectories for 20 films (thicknesses 7-25 sigma, three cutoff radii, two temperatures): the root-mean-square residual is 0.001-0.002 epsilon/sigma^3, against 0.010-0.021 for the uncorrected profile, and Q, the amount that the contour choice transfers between the two interfaces of a film with non-equivalent surfaces, is recovered to within 0.6% of the surface tension. Applied to the normal component, the same closure removes 83-92% of the spurious structure of the per-atom zz profile, a test that needs no IK run. Its mixture form is validated on three two-component films with an adsorbate unequally distributed between their faces, where it resolves the tension of each face; a clean face recovers the tension of the pure film.

papers.title: Second-order Bethe-Salpeter kernels: the interplay of vertex-corrected quasiparticle energies and the screened interaction
papers.abstract: We study second-order Bethe-Salpeter kernels generated by truncating an iterative formulation of Hedin's equations after the second cycle. Starting from the Hartree-Fock or the $GW$ self-energy, whose first cycles correspond to TDHF and $GW$+BSE, we obtain the second-cycle kernel by differentiating the first-cycle correlation self-energy with the interacting correlation function replaced by the non-interacting one, and evaluate it in the static limit of the effective kernel. Using fixed restricted Hartree-Fock orbitals, we benchmark 30 singlet and 28 triplet excitation energies for seven small molecules (six for the triplets) against the theoretical best estimates from QUEST v1.2. The second cycle lowers the mean absolute error (MAE) in both sequences. For the $GW$ sequence, the MAE decreases from 0.63 to 0.29 eV (singlets), on par with ADC(2) (0.30 eV), and from 0.43 to 0.38 eV (triplets). BSE$^{(2)}$@HF removes the triplet instabilities of TDHF and yields MAEs of 0.43 and 0.38 eV, or 0.31 and 0.30 eV when the Tamm-Dancoff approximation is applied in all cycles. Assigning the statically screened interaction $W_0$ to the exchange part of the $GW$ self-energy counts second-order screening twice in the second-cycle kernel and strongly blueshifts valence excitations. Without this double counting, dressing the exchange-type terms with $W_0$ lowers the singlet MAE from 0.37 to 0.29 eV but leaves the triplets nearly unchanged. Replacing second-order Green's function (GF2) quasiparticle energies by vertex-corrected ones in the same kernel raises excitation energies by about 0.7 eV, improving Rydberg but degrading valence excitations. A perturbative dynamical correction of the kernel blueshifts valence excitations by 0.3-0.4 eV and increases the errors of all full-matrix BSE$^{(2)}$ variants. The consistent improvement over the first cycle suggests that higher cycles are worth pursuing.

papers.title: Electronic-Structure-Informed Many-Body Encoding for Quantum Machine Learning
papers.abstract: Data encoding is a central challenge in quantum machine learning (QML), as it determines how classical information is mapped onto quantum states and influences the expressive power and efficiency of parameterized quantum circuits. Here, we introduce a physics-informed quantum encoding strategy that exploits the intrinsic many-body structure of electronic systems to establish a direct correspondence between the body order of input descriptors and the locality of quantum gates. Specifically, $n$-body electronic descriptors obtained from a single mean-field electronic-structure calculation are encoded through $n$-qubit gates, yielding a systematic hierarchy of quantum circuits with increasing many-body expressivity. Using reduced-density-matrix descriptors, we construct quantum machine-learning models incorporating one- through four-body encodings and benchmark their performance in predicting electron-correlation energies along bond-stretching potential energy surfaces. We demonstrate that increasing the body order of the encoding systematically improves prediction accuracy toward the full configuration interaction limit. Remarkably, disconnected many-particle densities constructed from lower-order electronic information achieve accuracy comparable to explicitly correlated two-particle densities in key cases, providing a computationally inexpensive route to higher-body quantum encodings. These findings establish a connection between the many-body structure of classical data and the design of quantum feature maps, offering a systematic, physically interpretable framework for enhancing the expressivity and predictive performance of quantum machine-learning circuits.

papers.title: Grow, Compress, and Perturb: A Hybrid Quantum-Classical Pathway to Scalable Quantum Chemistry on Quantum Computers
papers.abstract: While Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE) variants are among the leading candidates for electronic structure calculations on quantum computers, gradient-based operator selection limits their scalability. To solve this, we introduce the Hamiltonian-gradient-free VULCAN (Variational Upbuilding, Layered Compression, Adaptive N-body perturbation) layered VQE framework. Our method dynamically generates ansatz operators using Variational Double Bracket Flow (VDBF) equations. Combined with a linearly scaling minimal complete pool, it creates a pool 4-12 times smaller than QEB (Qubit-Excitation-Based) pools. By appending entire layers simultaneously, Hamiltonian gradient measurements are completely eliminated. Circuit depth is managed via a grow-then-compress scheme using efficient state-overlap measurements, and qubit requirements are reduced by projecting the Hamiltonian onto a dominant-determinant subspace. Using high-performance emulation up to 32 logical qubits, we achieve chemical accuracy at just 5-20% of the measurement cost of batched ADAPT-VQE for hydrogen chains, BeH2 and H2O. For the 32-qubit C3H6, where batched ADAPT-VQE does not reach chemical accuracy, a single VULCAN layer combined with a GPU-accelerated stochastic Epstein-Nesbet (ENPT2) correction does. This stochastic ENPT2 post-processing step enables early termination at chemical accuracy.

papers.title: Where Does the Anion-Redox Hole Go? Reliability of Open-Shell Projection-Based Embedding for Li-Rich Cathodes, from DFT Environments to Quantum Solvers
papers.abstract: Anion redox in Li-rich layered oxides places holes on oxygen next to an antiferromagnetic Mn(IV) d3 lattice, a strongly correlated open-shell problem for which projection-based wavefunction-in-DFT embedding offers a route to correlated and quantum solvers, but whose errors are known mainly for closed-shell molecules. We develop a spin-unrestricted projection-based embedding, exact at the DFT-in-DFT level to the microhartree scale for closed-shell, broken-symmetry and high-spin references with point charges, and apply DMRG-in-DFT to point-charge clusters of delithiated Li(2-x)MnO3, varying the environment functional (0-100% exact exchange), geometry, active region, active-space spin, virtual space, cluster size and magnetic reference. In every setting the lowest SCF state places the hole on an oxygen pair, with no O-O bond. How the hole is shared depends on the functional together with the geometry: hybrids give a full, uncoupled hole at the DFT+U geometry but a partial, weakly covalent hole at their own geometry, a change of up to 0.5 e on one oxygen. Where spin spreads across the active/environment boundary, the integer spin projection of the active space becomes a choice worth up to 0.26 e, and at most 0.09 e once the two Mn neighbors are included. An extended state search found missed lower states for two functionals, changing a pair-oxygen spin by up to 0.45 e. Across all 82 runs the embedded mean field gives the same hole (median DMRG change 0.02-0.04 e); correlation mainly adds O-O covalency. State control and geometry consistency, not the solver, dominate the uncertainty, and total energies are not converged at 30-40 orbitals. For quantum solvers, the embedded Hamiltonian must be spin-unrestricted: a shared-orbital form reverses the hole, while sample-based quantum diagonalization reproduces exact diagonalization, as accurately as, but not better than, classical selected CI.

papers.title: FermiLink: An Agent Harness for Multidomain Scientific Simulations
papers.abstract: Artificial-intelligence (AI) agent harnesses have been developed for autonomous scientific simulations, but most current agent harnesses are tested on single or a small set of software packages. Herein, FermiLink, an extensible open-source agent harness is introduced for multidomain scientific simulations. Its key design principle is the separation of package knowledge bases from simulation workflows, so that simulation workflows in FermiLink, from figure-level simulations to full-paper-level research on high-performance computing clusters, operate uniformly among supported packages via a four-layer progressive disclosure mechanism. This agent harness is specifically optimized for high performance computing (HPC) clusters, enabling multi-day multi-step scientific simulations in the absence of human intervention. Using OpenAI Codex as the agent provider, the capabilities of FermiLink are demonstrated across approximately 50 scientific software packages spanning nine research domains from chemistry to engineering. Systematic benchmarks on 132 real-world figure-level reproduction tasks with 44 packages show that FermiLink reproduces 74 (56.1%) of published figures with simulations, among which 30 (22.7%) achieve high-fidelity agreement and 35 reach qualitative agreement with the target figures. A smaller set of human expert-guided reproduction benchmarks with 10 packages in physics and chemistry further highlights the importance of expert insights for improving the simulation fidelity. Beyond reproduction, a single-blinded study demonstrates that FermiLink can produce research-grade results on unpublished polariton physics problems when provided with sufficiently detailed research objectives. Overall, FermiLink provides a scalable research infrastructure that may accelerate the path from scientific questions to computational results across diverse domains.

papers.title: Quaternion Dirac--Coulomb--Breit Integral Transformation for Relativistic Four-Component Correlated Electronic Structure Theory
papers.abstract: High-accuracy correlated four-component relativistic electronic structure methods are typically formulated in terms of integrals over molecular orbital (MO). Consequently, an efficient and scalable strategy is required to deal with the complexity of transforming relativistic two-electron integrals from the atomic orbital (AO) to the MO basis. The transformation bottleneck is particularly acute for approaches that include Breit interaction integrals, whose computational and memory demands further exacerbate the transformation cost. To overcome this challenge, we develop a quaternion-based, AO-driven direct integral transformation scheme. The method operates on scalar AO integrals and combines quaternion density-based contractions with direct Cauchy-Schwarz screening to systematically exploit integral locality. As a result, the proposed framework substantially lowers the practical computational scaling and provides an efficient, memory-conscious, and highly parallelizable pathway for the routine inclusion of relativistic Dirac-Coulomb-Breit integrals in large-scale four-component correlated calculations.

papers.title: Putting PASPT2 on a Firmer Basis
papers.abstract: The recently proposed partial-active-space (PAS) multi-state second-order perturbation theory (PASPT2) [Precis. Chem. 4, 997 (2026)] features connected amplitudes and a connected, closed intermediate Hamiltonian. Despite these hallmarks, PASPT2 (denoted as PASPT2H from now on) is not strictly size-extensive, as originally thought (and numerically confirmed), albeit strictly size-consistent. Nevertheless, PASPT2 is near-extensive for the states with major projections on the chosen PAS $\mathcal{M}_0$. This becomes more transparent upon introducing PASPT2X, a strictly size-extensive variant. Compared with the intruder-prone PASPT2X, the intruder-free PASPT2H merely neglects the second-order corrections that are important only for those states with major projections on the orthogonal complement $\mathcal{R}_X$ of $\mathcal{M}_0$ within the closed space $\mathcal{M}_X$ ($=\mathcal{M}_0\oplus\mathcal{R}_X$); however, such states are not supported by the chosen finite one-particle basis set. The weak violation of size-extensivity is therefore numerically insignificant for the target states supported by $\mathcal{M}_0$, reinforcing the theoretical basis of PASPT2H.

papers.title: Chiral vibrational modes and vibrational circular dichroism
papers.abstract: The recent interest in chiral phonons in a variety of physical phenomena and their hypothesized role in the chiral-induced spin selectivity effect [Phys. Rev. Research, 5, L022039 (2023)] call for further investigation into the chirality of molecular vibrations. Although molecular chirality has conventionally been quantified using structural properties, recent work has highlighted the role of dynamical response properties as chirality metrics. In this work, we examine an inter-atom helicity pseudoscalar as a complementary measure of vibrational chirality, associated with the vibrational circular dichroism (VCD) intensity in the fixed partial charge (FPC) approximation. This pseudoscalar is translationally and rotationally invariant, can distinguish between opposite enantiomers, and unlike an atomic pseudoscalar measure considered in our earlier work [Phys. Rev. Lett., 133, 268001 (2024)] does not rely on a predefined symmetry axis. For a twisted ethane model as well as several small molecules, this pseudoscalar correlates well with structural descriptors based on the continuous chirality measure. Overall, our results support response-based metrics as a physically meaningful and practically useful characterization of vibrational chirality. Importantly, while the FPC-based VCD estimate provides a useful quantifier of vibrational chirality, we show that it is a rather poor predictor of the actual molecular VCD response because the latter is strongly influenced by the (vibrational configuration-dependent) molecular electronic response.

papers.title: Learning the information contained in the microstructure of data distributions
papers.abstract: Understanding how much and where information is nested in sets of data obtained using different parameters and metrics is a typical problem in the analysis of high-dimensional datasets. Approaches based on relative data-driven metrics may be poorly quantitative and difficult to interpret, while accurate methods may be computationally expensive and impractical for large datasets. Here, we report an efficient, quantitative, and transferable method useful to this end, which we call "Micro-Information Analysis". Its foundation is based on the tight relationship that exists between the microscopic features of data distributions and the information they contain. The method performs preliminary unsupervised clustering, capturing microstructural features of data distributions such as the dominant Gaussian microdomains (microstates) present in them, their population, separation, and their residual non-Gaussian fraction. Leveraging the principle of clustering-and-minimization of Shannon entropy, this allows quantifying in bit (that is, in absolute metric) the information contained in the microstructure of the data, and how much information is nested in each Gaussian and non-Gaussian microdomain. The output of the analysis is a set of easily interpretable Information-Microstructure plots that allow to readily compare and rank data based on their information content and to graphically map the information breakdown among their various microenvironments in diagrams that are easy to interpret. We prove the efficiency of our method by analyzing and ranking data generated synthetically or from molecular simulations, demonstrating how "Micro-Information Analysis" is a physically-grounded quantitative tool useful for the study of physical systems from their data and for data science in general.
